## Overview

The PR simplifies `mount()` by inlining the message callback and changes `unmount()` to only clear `this.socket`. This removes the stored handler reference previously used for listener cleanup.

**Risk area:** `unmount()` no longer detaches the listener, so sockets can continue invoking `render()` after unmount; repeated mounts may accumulate listeners and retain the view. Lifecycle and resource-cleanup specialists should review this closely.

## Strengths

- Keeps message handling behavior intact while mounted.
- The diff is small and narrowly scoped.

## Candidate evidence

- **P1/P2 — Listener leak and stale callbacks:** `socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))` creates an unremovable handler, while `unmount()` removes the prior `off(...)` call. Unmounted or remounted views can continue receiving messages.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This PR simplifies `SocketView`'s lifecycle in `src/socket-view.ts`: `mount()` now registers an inline anonymous arrow listener (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`) instead of storing it in `this.onMessage`, and `unmount()` drops the previous `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` call in favor of just clearing `this.socket`.

The stated intent is to "refine behavior while preserving existing contracts," but the change breaks the teardown contract: the listener is no longer detachable or detached. While mounted, message handling is unchanged, but after `unmount()` the socket still holds and invokes the anonymous callback, and nothing ever removes it.

## Verification

Verification was disabled: `pr_review_verify` discovery found no user-level `verificationBaselines` configured (`enabled: false`, no candidate names), so no baseline was run. Verification executes PR code unsandboxed (no filesystem/network sandbox; supervision signals only the original POSIX process group), and is enabled only by a trusted user-level profile with explicit risk acknowledgement. Findings below rest on direct source inspection of both base and head versions instead.

## Findings

### [P1] Restore message-listener deregistration in unmount
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** `mount()` registers an anonymous closure (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`) and discards the only reference to it, while `unmount()` now only does `this.socket = undefined` — the `off("message", this.onMessage)` teardown was deleted. Three concrete consequences, each triggered by ordinary usage:
- **Render after unmount:** any `"message"` emitted after `unmount()` still calls `this.render(...)` on the unmounted view, whose socket reference is already cleared.
- **Listener accumulation:** each `mount()` on the same (long-lived) socket adds a new listener and removes none, so mount/unmount cycles produce duplicate renders per message.
- **Memory retention:** the socket retains the closure, which captures `this`, keeping every "unmounted" `SocketView` unreachable-by-`unmount` but unreachable-for-GC while the socket lives.

The base version (`main`: `this.onMessage = ...; socket.on("message", this.onMessage);` … `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)`) cleaned up correctly, so this is a regression introduced by this diff. Fix by storing the handler again (or using a bound method) and calling `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` in `unmount()` before clearing `this.socket`.
**Location:** `src/socket-view.ts:18 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed. (6/6 passes returned semantically complete; 0 partial, 0 timed out, 0 failed.)

## Strengths and notes

- The change is small and narrowly scoped, and mounted-state behavior (routing each message to `render`) is preserved.
- Correctness: confirmed lifecycle regression — cleanup contract of `unmount()` is broken (the P1 above).
- Security: a long-lived or attacker-driven socket can amplify CPU/memory via accumulated stale handlers; this is the same root defect, not a separate vulnerability.
- Performance: the closure retention is the memory/resource side of the same fix; no additional hot-path regressions found.
